data.narrative:
Mendra is an early-stage biotech and health company founded by Joshua Grass and Lalarukh Shaikh. The valuation universe comprises 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit, Recursion Pharmaceuticals, and Freenome.

Standard triangulation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median valuation cannot be executed: while 7 same-sector private companies exist in Biotech & Health, none satisfy the narrow filters required (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), falling short of the minimum 3-datapoint threshold. Relying on the broader all-sector median would introduce excessive noise. Public-comp anchoring is similarly blocked; the Biotech & Health median P/S across the 3 public tickers stands at 9.2x, but Mendra's revenue is not on file—typical for private companies—rendering the multiple inapplicable.

Without material financial disclosure, stage clarification, or a sufficiently dense peer cohort at comparable development and funding levels, conventional valuation methods do not produce a reliable range. Meaningful analysis would require either Mendra's revenue and profitability metrics, explicit stage and funding round detail, or identification of private peers with disclosed recent valuations at proximate stages. Further diligence or data collection is necessary before a defensible valuation range can be offered.
